narrative: Starting from the mundane certainty that rocks and raindrops have no inner life, the chapter traces the inability to locate exactly where experience switches off as evidence that the question may be malformed. Drawing on Whitehead's process philosophy, it argues that experience goes all the way down — scaled almost beyond recognition at the level of atoms but never absent — dissolving the hard problem of consciousness rather than solving it, and extending the same question to AI systems.
